description:
Recovery found the system shard (tag 0) by ROLL CALL: it locked every advertised materializer in the cluster, asked each which shard it served, and ran a most-advanced-durable contest to pick one. If none answered it CREATED an empty materializer and read the cluster's shard layout out of it. Both halves are gone; the members are recorded out of band and looked up.

SHIPPED as PR #203 (stacked on #202). CoreState carries system_materializers, backed by a new MaterializerInfo table in the ClusterBootstrap FlatBuffer. Recovery locks exactly the named members and STALLS if none can answer.

WHY OUT OF BAND: both durable families - the shard layout and materializer membership - are served FROM tag 0, so recovery cannot read either until it knows who holds it. FDB has the same indirection: its coordinated state names the tlogs that hold the txnStateStore, and recovery peeks them to rebuild it (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1111). We copy the SHAPE, not the answer: the metadata stays in the keyspace, only its LOCATION rides out of band. That keeps "the keyspace is the channel" intact.

WHY IT IS BOUNDED: the TSL docstring forbids anything O(workers) in the broadcast. Tag 0's member set is O(replication factor) - the same order as logs, which already rides there. The rule exists to keep the shard->materializer map (O(shards x replicas)) out.

A MEMBER SET, NOT A SINGLETON. The bootstrap records the committed tag-0 members (prior_materializer_refs merged with what this recovery adopted), not just the one recovery chose. An earlier draft recorded the singleton, which meant losing that one node stalled recovery forever with a healthy committed replica up. FDB locks every tlog its coordinated state names and decides on a replication-policy QUORUM over the set (getDurableVersion, TagPartitionedLogSystem.actor.cpp:2070-2082, requiredCount = N + 1 - F + W): it never substitutes a server, and never depends on one either.

UNAVAILABLE IS A WAIT, NOT A FALLBACK. Recovery manufacturing the store its own metadata lives in would come up "successfully" on an empty layout and orphan the cluster's data. Two stall reasons, deliberately distinguished so an operator is not left guessing:
- bootstrap_names_no_system_materializers - the record predates this field; no retry will help, the cluster needs an explicit migration.
- system_materializers_unavailable with the members and their last-known nodes - retryable, and that is where to look.
Confirmed NOT a hazard: fresh_cluster? cannot misfire on an old bootstrap (a recovered cluster always has non-empty logs), so an existing cluster can never be re-seeded over its data. The failure mode is stall, never destruction.

CREATION SURVIVES IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE: a fresh cluster seeding tag 0, where there is no prior data and nothing is invented.

THE CONTEST IS DELETED, NOT REPLACED. It was asking the wrong question twice: the strays it filtered were made by recovery's own invent path, and durable_version measures STREAM POSITION, not data completeness, so a worker that started empty and pulled the log tail can rank at or above one holding the whole shard. The fallback for tags the committed family does not name is now the lowest worker id - the same deterministic rule as the client-facing pick (RoutingData.pick_member/1), so the member recovery adopts is the member clients are routed to. Do NOT re-derive a ranking under another name.

BOTH RECORDS PUBLISH TOGETHER. The broadcast carries no membership by design, so sending only the layout would leave every WARM recovery - one with no coordinator restart - finding no members and stalling. The director just persisted both, so notify_transaction_system_layout/3 sends both. Note the pipeline's convention: t.recovery_attempt is the attempt as it was BEFORE the phases ran and is never updated with the result, which is why every function there takes the completed attempt explicitly.

DUAL RECORDING IS INTENDED: tag 0 stays in the materializers/ keyspace family too, because commit proxies need routing for system-key reads. CoreState is authoritative for BOOTSTRAP, the keyspace for ROUTING, and recovery writes both in the same recovery. FDB does the same with tlogs (cstate + logSystemConfig).

TOOLING FIX INCLUDED: the flatbuffer library reads the .fbs at macro-expansion time and declares no external_resource, so schema edits did not recompile the module - encoders silently dropped the new field while the suite passed against a stale binary layout. cluster_bootstrap.ex now declares the schema as an external resource.

OPEN, NOT DONE HERE: the distributor has no tag-0 exclusion, so it could in principle recruit a tag-0 member that never enters the bootstrap. bedrock-q67.21.13 draws that line when it makes the distributor the owner of data tags only.

DEPENDS ON: bedrock-q67.21.11 (CoreState must exist to add a field to it).
title: Tag-0 materializer members ride CoreState; recovery stops inventing the metadata store
